rule: near-send-gate-rule (the maintainer 2026-11-06): block only on evidence; a check that couldn't run asks once per (record, reason); a seal-holding soft state never shows 'send without encryption'; the gate never reads the audits index.
baseline: a verified near.ai record with the model key bound in a verified quote, DCAP up to date, NVIDIA verified, TLS verified, trust scope bound and matching, provenance all verified

quotePolicyRule: S37 (the maintainer 2026-11-08, freeze item B, near.ai inference-sdk ff591054 policies): teemoon's own checks, before and beside dcap-qvl. quote:debug — a TD quote (gateway, model, GPU node or compose manager) whose TDATTRIBUTES byte 0 bit 0 (TUD.DEBUG) is set is evidence, whether or not Intel answers. reportData:mismatch — a report_data field the gateway or a model node advertises that is not the quote's own report_data is evidence (absent: nothing to compare). modelMrConfig:mismatch — a model node quote whose mr_config is not 0x01 ‖ sha256(app_compose) of the compose it served is evidence, read as the gateway's code identity. nras:absent — a near.ai model node that answered with a quote but no nvidia_payload couldn't be checked: an outage, it asks, never verified, never blocks; the degraded reason and the confirm key are 'the model's hardware attestation is unavailable.'; the GPU row reads 'no nvidia evidence in this attestation' (freeze A2, the maintainer 2026-11-08). modelQuote:absent (1.1.1, audit v1.1.0-6c5f7a2 LOW 'a model key with no quote behind it'): a model attestation with a 32-byte key and no quote the parser can read is evidence; the key is unproven, so the send blocks, never 'still checking' with send anyway. candidates (C3, docs/NEARAI_SDK_C.md): every enclave in the gateway's model_attestations[] for the model must carry the sealed key, a quote that verifies with that key and our nonce in report_data, pass teemoon's quote checks, commit mr_config to its own app_compose, and replay its boot log; any failure is evidence (keyDiffers/keyNotInQuote read as an unbound key). keyProviderDiffers (1.1.1, audit A13): one key means one key service, so a listed enclave whose boot log names a key provider or mr-kms other than the first listed enclave's is evidence (a split list marks every enclave unlike the first; none on any enclave is nothing to compare). A list that never came is a couldn't-check. listedDcap (1.1.1, audit interim 2026-11-20): each listed enclave's quote also goes through the same DCAP path as the model node's (dcap-qvl: QE report bound to the PCK chain, collateral, TCB policy), gated the same way: failure or a TCB outside the allow-list is evidence, Intel unreachable is a couldn't-check, pending holds the send. The local parse checks the QE report too: its signature under the PCK leaf and report_data = sha256(attestation key || QE auth data), so a body signed by a key the quote carries itself is never verified, Intel answering or not. listedScope (1.1.1, audit A4): each listed enclave's entry also goes through the read enclave's trust scope, on its own quote and the list's nonce: the compose manager's quote binds its action log (DCAP on that quote, same TD, TCB verdicts agree), its boot event log replays to its RTMR3 and commits to its compose, and its running files match their pins. A mismatch is evidence, with the read enclave's reason lines. Intel unreachable for the compose manager's quote is a couldn't-check (stillChecking, the read enclave's reason). No compose-manager quote or no boot event log is a couldn't-check, never clean ('the model's hardware attestation is unavailable.'). An absent advertised report_data needs nothing: the quote's own report_data is checked against key || nonce directly. Residual: enclaves the key service admits but near.ai doesn't list are not checked.
confirmScopeRule: F4 (formal model): a 'send anyway' confirms one (record, reason) — the record by its fetchedAt and nonce; the reason is the degrade reason whenever one is known (a couldn't-check, policy confirm), even while other checks still run (F4 strict, the maintainer 2026-11-07: one answer covers the record), and 'pending' only when no reason is known yet. The gate after prepareTurn accepts only a confirmation for the record and reason it reads then; anything else asks (pending) or refuses (a soft reason); block is never accepted.
pendingRule: S30 (the maintainer 2026-11-07, 'no message leaves while the chip reads verifying'): a send waits, up to the settle timeout (15 s), for every pending kind: a hardware verdict (DCAP, NVIDIA, TLS, trust scope), a record older than attestationMaxAge (600 s) whose refetch is in flight (the send then goes to the NEW record's key), the near.ai tier unknown, and image provenance in flight. Still pending at the timeout, a sealed send asks: provenance alone asks 'provenancePending' (send anyway / wait), any other kind asks 'stillChecking' (send anyway / wait). 'send anyway' confirms (record, reason): reason 'pending' for the hardware kinds, 'provenancePending' for provenance alone; neither covers the other. 'wait' declines the held turn: nothing is sent, a fresh send's question returns to the composer. A failed refetch of a stale record is outage/near-ai-stale-record. Shortcuts has no one to ask: it refuses while anything is pending. ask: stillChecking | provenancePending; answer outcome: proceedSealed | nothingSent.
pcsStatusRule: the maintainer 2026-11-06 'yes block', exact split: 400, 404 and 422 are hard only on the requests built from the quote's own fields, TCB info by FMSPC (tcb) and the PCK CRL by CA (pckcrl); a forged quote with an unregistered FMSPC never reaches 'send anyway'. Every other status on those, and any status on QE identity or the root CA CRL, is unchecked (ask). status -1 = no HTTP response or a timeout. A quote whose fields can't form the request is hard before any fetch; an unreadable 2xx body is unchecked.
nrasTlsRule: near-gate-nvidia-tls-split (the maintainer 2026-11-06): an NVIDIA or TLS check that can't reach its server (network down, timeout, server error) is an outage: orange row, ask once. Malformed evidence from near.ai (an unreadable GPU evidence blob or TLS quote, a wrong-length key field, a bad fingerprint, missing TLS fields) and an unrecognised NVIDIA answer are evidence: red row, block. teemoon's own fault (it lost the request nonce, couldn't build the address) is orange, asks, and its detail is the approved line 'this check failed inside teemoon, so it proves nothing.'. class: outage | evidence | teemoon. Added 2026-11-06 (the maintainer): an NRAS signing key missing from NVIDIA's key set after one refetch is an outage (rotation on NVIDIA's side); no captured server certificate is an outage; a captured certificate whose public key can't be read is evidence. A certificate with an unsupported key type would be teemoon's fault, but the fingerprint hashes the whole SubjectPublicKeyInfo whatever the key type, so that case does not arise. reasonLine (2026-11-06): on a teemoon fault the degraded reason, the GPU row and the TLS row say the fault line itself, never "(service unreachable)" or "could not complete". unpublished+… vectors (TLA+ finding F1): an unpublished image exempts only itself from the gate; any other evidence still blocks and any other outage still asks.
